newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rexrodt says Krupp-Thyssen steel merger inevitable.
newsitem.headline: Rexrodt says Krupp-Thyssen steel merger inevitable.

text.p: German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Friday that merging the steel operations of industry giants Krupp and Thyssen was unavoidable in the medium term.

Speaking at a coal industry conference, Rexrodt also said the talks for a mutually acceptable deal between Fried. Krupp AG Krupp-Hoesch and Thyssen AG were clearly going well. The two have begun talks on creating a joint steel company after Krupp suspended a hostile takeover bid.
Rexrodt says steel merger eventually unavoidable
"The goal of all efforts must be to strengthen the competitiveness of the German steel industry and to secure jobs," Rexrodt said. "Germany must keep its steel base."
Rexrodt also said Bonn would offer aid to help ease dependence on coal and steel jobs in the depressed industrial areas of the Ruhr and Saar.

The Deutsche Ausgleichsbank and the Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau development agency would offer 900 million marks in low-interest credit in the region over the next three years, he said. Companies would receive 50,000 marks in credit for each new job created.
Workers would be able to cover 100 percent of retraining costs wtih loans with an interest rate of 4.75 percent, he said. Bonn would also provide financial support for two retraining centres.
